_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the only thing that ever promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, behind its own pull request — see that file's own doc comment for why the human checkpoint lives there instead of here. Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved' (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). A human's actual review happens by reading/merging the review agent's PR, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Clark Art (155 Ashley Road, Hale) closed permanently on 3 October 2024 after 18 years, per Bill Clark's own retirement announcement (reported by Altrincham Today, 'An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village'). The prior research pass's sources (Tripadvisor/Artsy/halebarns.com listings) were stale directory pages that hadn't been updated to reflect the closure. Do not re-suggest — the gallery no longer exists.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Yang Sing (34 Princess Street) has been closed since December 2021/early 2022 (kitchen fire, then a lease dispute) and Yang Sing Limited is now in liquidation per Companies House — it never reopened despite the owner's 2022 hope to reopen by 2023/24. The prior research pass's sources (visitmanchester.com, Hardens, Tripadvisor) were stale listings still showing it as an open, operating restaurant. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Blue Lobster
suggestions.reason: Italian seafood on the corner of London Road and Brown Street, sourced directly from Rome — a Franciacorta bar downstairs, the kitchen running until midnight upstairs.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Blue Lobster (34 London Road, Alderley Edge) closed permanently in December 2017, less than nine months after its April 2017 opening, following a staff-payment dispute with owner Andrea Zecchino (reported by alderleyedge.com and Manchester Confidential at the time). No evidence of any reopening or trading activity was found in the eight years since. The prior research pass's Tripadvisor/Luxury Lifestyle Magazine sources were leftover listings from the 2017 opening, not current confirmation. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Archive Bar & Bottle
suggestions.reason: Two floors on Mellor Road — real ale downstairs, a proper gin and cocktail list up top, and nobody rushing you between them.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA (camra.org.uk/pubs/archive-cheadle-hulme-167245), Tripadvisor 2026 reviews, and Facebook — a real, currently-trading two-floor bar at 2 Mellor Road, Cheadle Hulme SK8 5AU, independently owned by Will and Tina (per the venue's own Facebook copy: 'just your independent cocktail, wine, craft beer bar'). No sibling sites found anywhere — single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Fills Cheadle Hulme's Drink gap (the district had zero Drink-category venues before this). Coordinates are the postcode centroid (SK8 5AU), street-level precision. Type COCKTAIL BAR reused as the closest existing fit for a mixed real-ale/gin/cocktail bar — no single existing type captures all three, same imperfect-fit precedent as BAB NQ. Confidence: high.

suggestions.name: Thorn Grove Park
suggestions.reason: Seven and a half acres in the middle of the village — bowls green, open lawn, and nowhere near as busy as the postcode suggests.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified as a real, currently-maintained public park in Cheadle Hulme (7.6 acres, sports facilities including bowls/football/basketball courts) via multiple independent sources (mypacer.com park listings, Shutterstock dated photography, local property listings referencing it by name). A public park, not a commercial operator, so Hard rule 1's chain-footprint check doesn't apply — same treatment as The Carrs (Wilmslow) already in venues.json. Closes Cheadle Hulme's total Do-category gap (zero Do venues before this). New type introduced: TOWN PARK — RIVERSIDE PARK (the only existing Do type mapped to the 'Parks & green space' tile) would be inaccurate here since Thorn Grove isn't riverside; flagging so the review/promotion step can decide whether to map TOWN PARK onto that tile too or leave it category-only like several other new types already in venues.json. Coordinates are street-level (postcode centroid), not per-building GPS. Confidence: high on the park being real and current; medium on precise coordinates given conflicting street-address noise in search results, but consistently the same postcode/lat-lon across independent sources.

suggestions.name: The Olde School
suggestions.reason: A converted schoolroom on the Village green, open four days a week for wholesome plates and coffee, with a wine list nobody expects from a place this size.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Companies House (The Olde School Ltd, company 15322463, incorporated Dec 2023, registered at The Estate Office, The Village, Prestbury SK10 4AL), Food Hygiene Ratings, and current Tripadvisor reviews describing it as a cosy independent cafe/eatery run by a named local owner. Single site, no chain footprint found anywhere — passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Fills Prestbury's Eat-category gap (the district had zero Eat venues before this; only two Drink venues, Bacchus and The Legh Arms). Type BRUNCH SPOT reused (fits the existing tile mapping and matches its actual offer — coffee, wholesome meals, wine, open 9-4 Tue-Sat). Coordinates are the postcode centroid (SK10 4AL), street-level precision. Confidence: high. Note: a separate Prestbury Do-category candidate (spa/gallery) was actively searched for and not found to a confident enough standard — Champneys at nearby Mottram Hall was found and rejected as a multi-site UK spa chain; a beauty salon (Prestbury Beauty) didn't read as a genuine 'Spa & wellness' tile fit. Prestbury's Do gap stays open rather than being padded.

suggestions.name: Oil Art Advisory Gallery
suggestions.reason: Zoe Garner's own two floors on King Street, opened 2024 — emerging names alongside the established, and nobody hurrying your second lap.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the gallery's own site (oilartadvisory.com), Own Art (ownart.org.uk), Discover Knutsford and Instagram — an independently-owned contemporary art gallery at 8 King Street, Knutsford WA16 6DL, founded March 2024 by gallerist Zoe Garner. No sibling locations found anywhere — single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Fills Knutsford's Do-category gap (the district had zero Do venues before this; only Drink/Eat). Coordinates are street-level, interpolated from nearby King Street listed-building coordinates (exact building-level lookup wasn't available), consistent with this file's existing street-level precision bar. Confidence: high on the venue being real, current and independent; medium on exact coordinate precision within King Street.

suggestions.name: Little Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: A basement on the George Street corner, twenty-odd years into the same Cantonese repertoire — the dim sum trolley Chinatown's newer rooms still measure themselves against.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via current (2026) Yelp, Tripadvisor and OpenTable listings showing live opening hours and recent reviews, plus The Good Food Guide — a real, currently-operating basement restaurant at 17 George Street, Manchester M1 4HE, on the corner with Charlotte Street, trading over 20 years. Distinct entity from 'Yang Sing' (34 Princess Street), which this file already rejected 2026-09-03 for closure/liquidation — Little Yang Sing is a separate, smaller sister restaurant with its own trading history, not the same closed business. One caution flagged and weighed: a Place North West report that the building (12 Charlotte Street/17 George Street) was sold by its charity landlord for £1.5m — read as an investment sale with the restaurant continuing as tenant, not a closure signal, and outweighed by multiple current 2026 reviews/live listings. New type introduced: DIM SUM — CANTONESE ROAST (Happy Seasons' type) doesn't capture the dim sum/yum cha repertoire specifically; left category-only (Eat) like other single-cuisine types already in this file (GREEK TAVERNA, VIETNAMESE etc). Confidence: medium-high, given the building-sale caveat above.

suggestions.name: Hale Wine Bar
suggestions.reason: Folding windows onto Ashley Road and a list built by someone who left the big pub groups to pour it properly.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Tripadvisor/Yelp 2026 listings (live opening hours, current reviews) and Altrincham Today's original opening coverage — an independent wine bar at 149 Ashley Road, Hale WA14 2UW, opened 2016 by Ashley Brown, previously operations director at a pub group, now running this as his own independent venture. No sibling sites found. Fills a real Hale gap — the district only had one Drink venue (The Elk of Hale, a cocktail bar) before this, no wine bar. Coordinates are the postcode centroid (WA14 2UW), street-level precision. Confidence: high.

suggestions.name: La Cucina
suggestions.reason: Wood-fired pizza and fresh pasta on London Road, cocktails at the same counter — the kind of independent Alderley Edge's chain-heavy strip could use more of.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Companies House (La Cucina Alderley Restaurant Limited, company 15410030, registered at 27A London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7JT), Tripadvisor 2026 reviews and the venue's own site (lacucinaeat.co.uk) — an independent wood-fired pizza, pasta and cocktail bar. Single-purpose registered company, no sibling sites found anywhere. Passes Hard rule 1 cleanly, and explicitly clears the ground already flagged as chain-heavy in this file's own notes: San Carlo (multi-city Italian chain) and Victors Alderley Edge (would duplicate the Hale Victors entry, already flagged) were both actively checked and excluded; The Alderley Restaurant (at Alderley Edge Hotel) was checked and excluded as JW Lees-brewery-owned, the exact same chain this file already excluded once for Stanneylands Hotel. Type PIZZERIA reused (same type/tile fit as Rudy's in Altrincham). Coordinates are the postcode centroid (SK9 7JT), street-level precision. Confidence: high.

suggestions.name: Dexter & Jones
suggestions.reason: A thousand beers and three hundred gins behind the counter, but it's Adam and Katy Rickitt's own wine picks worth pulling up a stool for.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA (camra.org.uk/pubs/dexter-jones-knutsford-173358), Companies House (Dexter & Jones Limited, company 09694876, active), and Pellicle magazine's 2024 feature — an independent bottle-shop-and-bar at 10 Princess Street, Knutsford WA16 6DD, owned and run by Adam and Katy Rickitt since 2015. One ambiguity actively checked: the venue's own website has a 'London' product-collection page, which reads as an online-store category (beers/spirits sourced from London producers, standard e-commerce navigation) rather than a second physical site — CAMRA, Tripadvisor and Pubs Galore all list a single physical location, none reference a London branch. No other physical sibling found. Fills a real Knutsford Do/Drink-adjacent gap (only Wallop existed as a wine-bar-type venue before this). Type WINE BAR reused as closest fit for a wine/beer/gin bottle-shop-bar, same imperfect-fit precedent as other hybrid bars in this file. Confidence: medium-high given the 'London' page ambiguity, resolved in the venue's favour on the weight of independent listing consensus.

suggestions.name: Contemporary Six Hale
suggestions.reason: Alex Reuben's second room, on Ashley Road in the space Clark Art left behind — contemporary names given the same quiet run of wall as the Manchester original.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the gallery's own site (contemporarysix.co.uk), which lists live exhibition dates through March-April 2026, plus Facebook — a real, currently-trading contemporary art gallery at 155 Ashley Road, Hale WA14 2UW, opened Dec 2024 as the second site of Manchester's Contemporary Six (founded 2010 by director Alex Reuben). Two-site footprint (Manchester + Hale) matches this file's own established precedent for a single sibling location (Craig's, Ivy Spinningfields) rather than the excluded multi-city pattern (Gagosian, Wally's). Note: shares its street address with 'Clark Art', which this file already rejected 2026-09-03 as permanently closed (Oct 2024) — Contemporary Six appears to have taken over the same space shortly after, which is corroborating evidence of the closure rather than a conflict. Fills Hale's Do-category gap (only Hale Country Club & Spa existed as a Do venue before this). Coordinates reused from the same Ashley Road postcode as Hale Wine Bar (both WA14 2UW), street-level precision. Confidence: high.

suggestions.name: Wong Wong Bakery
suggestions.reason: Twenty-plus years on Princess Street, family-run, and the egg tarts are usually gone by mid-afternoon on a Saturday.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via current (2026) Yelp/Tripadvisor listings with live opening hours, Manchester's Finest, and a themanc.com feature marking its 20th year trading — a real, currently-operating family-run Chinese bakery at 28-32 Princess Street, Manchester M1 4LB, established 2003. No sibling sites found anywhere. Fills Chinatown's Eat-category variety (currently only Happy Seasons, a Cantonese roast specialist) with a genuinely different register — a daytime bakery rather than a dinner room. Type BAKERY reused (same type as Pollen Bakery, Ancoats — maps to the 'Cafés (late)' tile, an imperfect but closest fit; a bakery-specific tile doesn't exist). Coordinates are street-level (Princess Street centroid). Confidence: high.
